senet.title: Senet
senet.description: The Game of Passing. A race across 30 squares to reach the afterlife.

legend.title: THE LEGEND OF THE TWILIGHT VOYAGE
legend.p1: Before the Great Pyramids touched the sky, the Scribes of Thoth recorded the first game of Senet. It is more than a diversion; it is a ritualistic map of the soul's perilous crossing through the Duat—the Egyptian underworld. Each board is a shadow of the cosmic order, where the journey from life to eternity is decided not just by skill, but by the favor of the gods.
legend.p2: Five 'Ba-souls' represent the fragments of your spirit, struggling to navigate the S-shaped path of existence. The sticks you cast are the breath of life; a 'perfect throw' signals the path is clear, while a 'miscast' leaves you vulnerable to the encroaching darkness. To move with a brother is to be shielded by Ma'at; to move alone is to invite the chaos of the void.
legend.p3: To win is to navigate the treacherous 'House of Water' and face the 'Three Truths' before finally ascending through the 'Gate of Horus' into the Field of Reeds. There, you shall join the Imperishable Stars and find eternal rest. To lose is to remain a wandering shadow, destined to repeat the cycle until your heart is light as a feather.

h26.title: House of Beauty
h26.desc: The sanctuary of ritual anointing. Here, the soul gathers its strength for the final trials of the afterlife.

h27.title: House of Water
h27.desc: The Abyssal Abode. A perilous void; failing to cross will wash your spirit back to the House of Rebirth (15).

h28.title: Hall of Three Truths
h28.desc: The first trial of the scales. Only a precise command of THREE will allow you to hold your ground.

h29.title: The Solar Bark
h29.desc: Joining the Sun God Re on his nocturnal voyage. A precise throw of TWO moves you toward the dawn.

h30.title: The Gate of Horus
h30.desc: The final threshold. A single precise step of ONE grants your spirit ascension into the eternal stars.

guide.title: SCROLL OF GUIDANCE
guide.objective: Guide all five of your spirit pieces off the board's edge to secure your place among the stars.
guide.movement: Travel the S-shaped path across thirty squares. The journey begins on the first row and ends at the threshold of eternity.
guide.throwing: Cast the four sticks to determine your fate (1–5 steps). Throws of 1, 4, or 5 are blessed by the gods, granting an extra turn.
guide.capturing: An isolated enemy is vulnerable. Land upon them to banish their soul back to your previous position.
guide.protection: A pair of brothers standing together is sanctified by Ma'at. They cannot be captured or displaced.
guide.blockades: Three or more pieces in a row form an impassable barrier, for no soul may leap over such a concentration of spirit.
guide.special: Squares 26 to 30 are the final gates. Beware Square 27 (Water), for falling there washes you back to the House of Rebirth (15).
guide.bearing_off: To pass the final threshold, you must roll the exact count needed to step beyond the final square.

lobby.about_body: Senet is not merely a board game, but a ceremonial race through fate itself. Two souls guide five pieces across a winding path, where every throw of the sticks may grant favor, invite peril, or open the road to immortality.
lobby.history_body: Born in the courts and tombs of ancient Egypt, Senet endured for millennia as both noble pastime and sacred symbol. In painted walls, carved boxes, and royal burials, it appears as a game played at the threshold between earthly life and the eternal Duat.

fun_facts.title: Fun Facts
fun_facts.fact_1: Senet boards were placed in tombs beside the dead, as though the contest might continue beyond the veil.
fun_facts.fact_2: Its final squares were understood as charged places of trial and blessing, where danger, judgment, and divine passage gathered at the board's edge.
fun_facts.fact_3: No single ancient rulebook survived, so the Senet played today is part scholarship, part restoration, and part reverent imagination.

mehen.title: Mehen
mehen.description: The Tradition of the Guarding Coil. Lions and balls race inward through a sacred spiral to claim the serpent's heart.

legend.title: THE LEGEND OF THE COILED SERPENT
legend.p1: In the deepest hours of the night, when the Sun God Re sails through the underworld, the great serpent Mehen coils around his bark. The serpent is protector, labyrinth, and sacred arena all at once, turning every inward step into a contest of nerve and favor.
legend.p2: Your balls race along the coils under the watch of a lion guardian. Some coils offer sanctuary, others invite sudden capture, and the lion's presence can turn a narrow path into a wall that only the worthy may cross.
legend.p3: This edition follows the Tradition of the Guarding Coil: every lion and every ball must press inward from the reserve box until all of them stand at the serpent's heart. Whoever completes that guarded ascent first wins Mehen's favor.

reserve.title: Reserve Box
reserve.desc: All lions and balls wait outside the spiral until a roll calls one of them onto the first coil.

safe.title: Guarded Coils
safe.desc: Coils 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 are protected places where a vulnerable ball may rest beyond capture.

lion.title: Lion's Wall
lion.desc: A lion can strike enemy balls and bar their passage, turning one narrow coil into a living barrier.

heart.title: Heart of Mehen
heart.desc: The spiral ends at Mehen's head, the seat of Ra. Every ball and the lion must reach this sacred center to win.

guide.title: SCROLL OF THE SERPENT
guide.objective: Guide your lion and all five balls from the reserve box through the serpent's coils until every one of them reaches the center.
guide.players: The Tradition of the Guarding Coil is strongest with two to four players, though this board supports up to six. Each player commands one lion and five balls.
guide.opening: Before the race begins, each player rolls once. The highest roll takes the first turn, then play continues clockwise around the board.
guide.setup: All lions and balls begin outside the board in the reserve box. The spiral itself is a sequence of guarded coils that begins at the outer edge and ends at Mehen's head in the center.
guide.entry: All pieces begin outside the board in the reserve box. On any roll, you may bring one off-board lion or ball onto coil 1 if it is unoccupied.
guide.turn: Play proceeds clockwise. On each turn, roll, choose one legal piece, move it, resolve any capture or protection effects, then check whether the roll grants an extra turn.
guide.movement: Each turn moves one piece forward exactly the value rolled. You must make a legal move if one exists; if none exists, your turn ends immediately.
guide.throwing: The Mehen throw produces values from 1 to 5. Rolls of 1 or 5 are blessed and grant an extra turn after your move.
guide.pieces: Balls are vulnerable pieces that may be captured and returned to the reserve. The lion is the strong piece: it may capture enemy balls, it cannot be captured by balls, and it can hold the path against them.
guide.capturing: Landing on an unprotected enemy ball captures it and sends it back to the reserve box. Landing on your own piece or on an enemy lion is not allowed.
guide.protection: A ball is protected when it rests on a safe coil or on a coil next to its own lion. Protected balls cannot be captured.
guide.safe_spaces: Coils 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 are safe coils. Any piece resting there is beyond capture for as long as it remains on that guarded place.
guide.blocking: A lion blocks the path of enemy balls. Opposing balls cannot pass through its coil, though enemy lions may still move beyond it.
guide.finishing: The center is the final coil. You must roll the exact number needed to enter it; overshooting the center makes that piece unable to move.
guide.no_legal_move: If the roll gives you no legal move at all, your turn ends at once. You may not pass voluntarily while a legal move remains.
guide.clarifications: Only one piece may occupy a coil at a time. Movement always follows the spiral inward; pieces never move backward except when a captured ball returns to the reserve.
guide.tie_rule: If more than one player completes the journey in the same round, the winner is the one who reached the center first.
guide.winning: You win only when all five balls and your lion have reached the center.

board.reserve_subtitle: Lions and balls wait here before entering the spiral.

lobby.about_body: Mehen is a spiral race played in the shelter of the serpent god. In the Tradition of the Guarding Coil, each player commands one lion and five balls, entering from the reserve box and pressing inward while safe coils, captures, and blocking lions turn the road to the center into a guarded ascent.
lobby.history_body: Ancient Mehen survives in carved spiral boards and scattered evidence rather than in one complete rulebook. This edition resolves that uncertainty by adopting a single house tradition, the Tradition of the Guarding Coil, and using it consistently across the papyrus, the lobby, and the board.

fun_facts.title: Serpent Lore
fun_facts.fact_1: Mehen boards were carved as snakes curled into dense spirals, making the board itself part icon and part race track.
fun_facts.fact_2: This edition keeps the surviving spiral form but fixes play around one consistent tradition: reserve entry, exact center rolls, lion blocking, and victory only when every piece reaches the heart.
fun_facts.fact_3: Safe coils at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 reflect the serpent's guarded rings, where even a vulnerable ball may rest beyond capture.

hounds-and-jackals.title: Hounds and Jackals
hounds-and-jackals.description: The Game of Fifty-Eight Holes. Five pegs per side race through marked jumps and setbacks toward the shen goal.

legend.title: THE LEGEND OF THE FIFTY-EIGHT HOLES
legend.p1: On carved boards shaped like an axe-head, noble players once guided pegs crowned with hounds and jackals through a field of carefully bored holes. The surviving boards tell us the path, but not every rule, so each modern game is part reconstruction and part reverent wager with the past.
legend.p2: This house papyrus imagines the board as a race of paired animal spirits. The hound and the jackal begin in reserve, answer the throw of four sticks, and press upward through marked holes that may either grant favor or pull a peg backward.
legend.p3: Victory in this telling comes not from battle but from steady passage. Guide all five pegs through the marked course, survive the setbacks, and enter the shining shen goal before your rival completes the same ascent.

good.title: Nefer Holes
good.desc: Marked favorable holes send a peg forward at once to a linked resting place farther up the board.

bad.title: Setback Holes
bad.desc: Some linked holes drag a peg backward the moment it lands, undoing part of the climb.

reserve.title: Reserve Pits
reserve.desc: Each side begins with five pegs waiting in reserve until a throw calls one onto the first hole.

goal.title: Shen Goal
goal.desc: The shared goal hole crowns the board. Every peg must reach it by exact count to complete the race.

guide.title: SCROLL OF THE FIFTY-EIGHT HOLES
guide.objective: Guide all five of your pegs from reserve to the shen goal before your rival does the same.
guide.players: This edition presents the two sides as Hound and Jackal, while preserving the same two-seat structure used across the app.
guide.setup: Each player begins with five pegs in reserve. No peg starts on the track, and the two races unfold on mirrored halves of the same board.
guide.entry: On any roll, you may bring one reserve peg onto the first hole if that final destination is not already occupied by one of your own pegs.
guide.movement: Choose one of your pegs and move it forward exactly the amount shown by the sticks. Pegs never capture or block the opposing side in this reconstruction.
guide.throwing: The four throw sticks produce values from 1 to 5, with the customary 0-light-sides result counting as 5.
guide.marked_holes: Certain holes are linked. Landing on one resolves its effect immediately and carries the peg to its linked destination.
guide.good_jumps: A favorable marked hole sends the peg forward, representing swift passage and good fortune on the board.
guide.bad_jumps: An unfavorable marked hole sends the peg backward. The move is still legal only if the linked resting hole is free of your own peg.
guide.stacking: Only one of your own pegs may occupy a hole. If a move would end on a hole already held by one of your pegs, it is illegal.
guide.finishing: The shen goal requires an exact count. Any roll that overshoots the goal leaves that peg unable to move.
guide.blocked_turns: If the current throw leaves you with no legal peg to move, the turn passes immediately to your opponent.
guide.winning: You win only when all five of your pegs have reached the shen goal.
guide.reconstruction_note: Because no single ancient rulebook survives, this implementation presents one consistent house reconstruction rather than claiming a definitive historical ruleset.

lobby.about_body: Hounds and Jackals is a Middle Kingdom race game built around fifty-eight drilled holes and animal-topped pegs. This edition treats it as a fast two-player contest of entry, timing, and marked jumps rather than as a game of capture.
lobby.history_body: Archaeological boards survive in elegant wooden and ivory forms, often with mirrored tracks and pegs crowned as hounds and jackals. The layout is clear, but the exact ancient rules are not, so modern play depends on careful reconstruction.

fun_facts.title: Board Lore
fun_facts.fact_1: Many surviving examples are shaped like an axe-head and drilled with fifty-eight holes, giving the game its modern nickname.
fun_facts.fact_2: The pegs themselves were often topped with animal heads, which is why the two sides are commonly described as hounds and jackals.
fun_facts.fact_3: This version declares itself a house reconstruction: exact finishing, linked good and bad holes, and no capture play.
